report.source_text: Written informed consent was provided by the patient after a comprehensive explanation of the procedures, and intravenous steroid pulse therapy, that is, a daily dose of 500 mg of methylprednisolone every 3 days per week for 2 weeks, and radiation therapy (20GY/10fr) was administered. After medical intervention, the imaging scans revealed no inflammation and her visual acuity recovered to 20/20; however, the right upper-eyelid retraction, that is, MRD-1, 5.9 mm, and hypertropia of 25PD remained.

clinician.final_diagnosis: Compressive Optic Neuropathy (CON) in the right eye due to Graves' ophthalmopathy, with inflammation and hypertrophy of the superior rectus and upper levator muscles.
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 66-year-old woman with a 23-year history of hyperthyroidism presented with right upper eyelid retraction. Initial examination showed no visual dysfunction. Three months later, her thyroid hormone control worsened (elevated FT4, FT3, TSAb), and her right upper eyelid retraction progressed. After an additional three months, she developed compressive optic neuropathy (CON) in her right eye, with significantly reduced visual acuity (20/200) and a central critical flicker fusion frequency of 16 Hz. Imaging (CT/MRI) confirmed a high degree of inflammation and hypertrophy specifically in the superior rectus and upper levator muscles. She was treated with intravenous steroid pulse therapy and radiation therapy, which led to resolution of inflammation on imaging and recovery of visual acuity to 20/20, though some eyelid retraction and hypertropia persisted.
